title: A `Core\Test` assertion outside a test grows the assertion ledger for the life of the program.
text: `Ctx::record_assertion` appends one entry per assertion, passing or failing, and nothing truncates the ledger outside a test. A `#[Test]` method owns an isolate that ends with it, so there the ledger is O(assertions in that test). Under `nvs run`, a `Core\Test` assertion in a loop adds one entry per call for as long as the program runs; `benches/members/lang/testing/assertions.nvs` declares that allocation. It is bounded by the memory ceiling, and `docs/reference/lang/95-testing.md` § *Assertions* says an assertion outside a test has no ledger to record it, which is true of the verdict and not of the storage. Closing it is recording nothing when no test owns the context, then a bench that ramps the assertion count under `nvs run` and pins a flat allocation.
